blocks: The people of the State of California do enact as follows:
It is the intent of the Legislature to enact subsequent legislation relating to conflicts of interest for all state employees and officers that would do the following:

(a) Prohibit any state officer or employee from owning or controlling any financial interest in a business or market sector regulated by their appointing authority or department unless written approval is granted by the appointing authority.

(b) Require every department to identify specific activities or financial interests that constitute a conflict of interest and submit the activities and interests to the Department of Human Resources for approval.

(c) Prohibit all state officers and employees from using their official position to influence decisions that benefit their financial interests or the financial interests of their family members; accepting gifts, gratuities, or other forms of compensation from entities regulated by or doing business with their department; or using state resources for personal gain or private advantage.

(d) Require exceptions to the prohibitions identified in subdivision (c) to be granted in writing by the head of the department or agency, subject to review and approval by the Department of Human Resources, and only when the financial interest or activity does not pose a material risk of influencing the employee’s duties or the public’s trust in the department’s objectivity.
(e) Require all state employees to annually file a statement of economic interest and disclose any changes in financial interest within 10 days.

(f) Require any state employee with disqualifying financial interest to recuse themselves from any decision, inspection, or enforcement action that materially affects those interests, and require every department to document and publicly disclose instances of recusal.

(g) Subject an employee who violates the conflict-of-interest provisions to disciplinary action, including termination of employment, and make void and unenforceable any agreement, decision, or contract made in violation of those provisions.

(h) Require every department to adopt policies to implement the conflict-of-interest provisions and require the Department of Human Resources to issue guidance to assist departments in developing and enforcing policies, including standardized procedures for reviewing and approving exceptions.
(i) Require the Fair Political Practices Commission to conduct periodic audits to ensure compliance by the departments.
digest: The Political Reform Act of 1974 regulates conflicts of interest of public officials and requires specified elected and appointed officers at the state and local levels of government to disclose specified financial interests by filing periodic statements of economic interests.

Existing law also prohibits a state officer or employee from engaging in any employment, activity, or enterprise that is clearly inconsistent, incompatible, in conflict with, or inimical to their duties as a state officer or employee and requires each appointing power to determine those activities. If those provisions are in conflict with a memorandum of understanding, existing law provides that the memorandum of understanding is controlling, except as specified.
This bill would express the intent of the Legislature to enact subsequent legislation relating to conflicts of interest for all state employees and officers, as specified.
label: Introduced
subject: State employees and officers: conflicts of interest.
title: An act relating to state employees.
